open_errors.issue: In ch 2 Rohan reads the warden report aloud: blood on the ice and 'a scrap of skin frozen fast to it, torn from the rim of an ear' (F383). Ch 22 (Meera POV) and ch 25 (Rohan POV) recall it as 'a curl of frozen cartilage no longer than a fingernail', which is the retired F063 wording.
open_errors.fix: Bring both recollections in line with the ch 2 report: a scrap of skin torn from an ear rim.

patches.find: Blood on the ice, and a curl of frozen cartilage no longer than a fingernail.
patches.replace: Blood on the ice, and a scrap of skin frozen fast to it, torn from the rim of an ear.

patches.find: He saw a cartilage curl in a warden's report, no longer than a fingernail.
patches.replace: He saw a scrap of frozen skin in a warden's report, torn from the rim of an ear.

open_errors.issue: The firewood count does not add up. Ch 10 ends with 24 dry sticks and the fever pot in ch 11 burns 4, which leaves 20. The night of ch 12 should then cost the usual five, leaving 15, but ch 13 dusk counts nineteen.
open_errors.fix: Have Meera note that the ch 12 night was carried on the wet deadfall plus one dry stick, which gives 20 - 1 = 19.

patches.find: "Nineteen," she said. "Five for the night. That leaves fourteen."
patches.replace: "Nineteen," she said. "The deadfall carried last night on one dry stick, and smoked us for it. Five for the night. That leaves fourteen."

open_errors.issue: In ch 24 Rohan counts to 160 with his forehead to the dry-stone wall at the foot of the walnut grove, while Meera hides the seal behind the goat shed. Ch 28 says he 'faced the wall' at the shed.
open_errors.fix: Put him back at the grove wall.

patches.find: At the shed he had faced the wall and counted to a hundred and sixty, and he had kept his word and never asked where.
patches.replace: At the grove wall he had faced the stones and counted to a hundred and sixty, and he had kept his word and never asked where.

open_errors.issue: In ch 31 Meera leaves Badami's big bell on its peg and says 'Bindu'll bring it.' In ch 32 she takes it from her own coat as 'the one she had lifted off the peg'.
open_errors.fix: Bindu brings the bell and hands it to Meera.

patches.find: Meera slid her good hand into her coat and brought out the bell.
patches.replace: Meera held out her good hand, and Bindu set the bell in it.

patches.find: It was the big bell, the one she had lifted off the peg by the salt-house stair
patches.replace: It was the big bell, the one Bindu had lifted off the peg by the salt-house stair

open_errors.issue: In ch 31 Meera chooses to be named on Rohan's writ and entered in the Closing Roll, rather than cross 'as a held name in my custody' (F378, F407). The ch 31 crossing confirms she travels as his named guide. In ch 32 she still calls herself 'a held name', and Rohan describes the held-name option as her status.
open_errors.fix: Reword so she is on the Roll and still unpardoned, with only the queen able to answer her Fair confession.

patches.find: "And until she says so," she said, "I'm a held name."
patches.replace: "And until she says so," she said, "I'm a name on her Roll and nothing more."

patches.find: "You are not pardoned. Your judgement waits in Taravan, and I cannot hand you a better answer than that. It is why we walk there together."
patches.replace: "You are not pardoned. The Roll bought your crew their peace, not your pardon. Only the queen can give that, and I cannot hand you a better answer than that. It is why we walk there together."
